title: Home & everyday objects
goal: Describe your home, say where things are (in, on, under, next to) and say what there is and isn't.
intro:
Gujarati expresses location with **postpositions** that follow the noun. The most common, **-માં** 'in', is written joined to the noun: ઘરમાં 'in the house'. Others, like **ઉપર** 'on', are written separately and often need **-ની** before them: ટેબલની ઉપર 'on the table'.

'There is' is simply **છે**, and 'there isn't' is **નથી**.

vocab.note: m · a fixture of Gujarati homes
n · વાસણ ધોવાં 'to wash the dishes'
m · પહેલે માળે 'on the first floor'

phrases.en: There are three rooms in my house.
The key is on the table.
Your bag is under the chair.
We live on the fourth floor.

phrases.native: બહાર બહુ ગરમી છે, અંદર આવો.
phrases.roman: bahār bahu garmī chhe, andar āvo.
phrases.en: It's very hot outside; come inside.

grammar.title: Postpositions: -માં, પર, and -ની + postposition
grammar.body:
Gujarati 'prepositions' come **after** the noun.

**-માં** *-māṃ* 'in' is written attached: ઘરમાં, ઓરડામાં, કબાટમાં.
**પર** *par* 'on' is written separately: ટેબલ પર.

Most others (**ઉપર, નીચે, પાસે, પાછળ, આગળ, સામે, બાજુમાં**) normally take **-ની** before them: ખુરશીની નીચે 'under the chair', ઘરની પાછળ 'behind the house'. With pronouns use the possessive feminine form: મારી પાસે 'near me / with me', તમારી સામે 'in front of you'.

**Oblique form:** before a postposition, masculine nouns in -o change to -ā, and neuter -uṃ nouns change to -ā: ઓરડો → ઓરડામાં, રસોડું → રસોડામાં.

examples.en: The book is in the bag.
The phone is on the bed.
The cat is under the table.
The shop is opposite my house.
The milk is in the kitchen.

grammar.title: 'There is / there isn't' and 'I have (with me)'
grammar.body:
Gujarati has no separate 'there is' — just put the place first and end with **છે** (singular or plural alike): **ઓરડામાં પંખો છે** 'There is a fan in the room'. The negative is **નથી**: **ઓરડામાં પંખો નથી** 'There's no fan in the room'.

**કોઈ** 'someone, anyone' and **કંઈ** 'something, anything': અંદર કોઈ છે? 'Is anyone inside?' — ના, કોઈ નથી 'No, nobody.'

For things you possess or carry, use **-ની પાસે** + છે: **મારી પાસે ગાડી છે** 'I have a car'.

examples.en: There's a window in the kitchen.
There's a swing in the house.
I don't have (any) money on me.

dialogue.title: Where are my keys?
dialogue.setting: Nisha is about to leave for work and can't find her keys. Her husband Amit helps.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: ના, ટેબલ પર ફક્ત મારો ફોન છે.
lines.roman: nā, ṭebal par fakt māro fon chhe.
lines.en: No, only my phone is on the table.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.en: They're not in the bag either.

lines.speaker: Amit
lines.en: On the swing? Or in the kitchen?

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.en: Oh, here they are! Under the swing.

culture: Many Gujarati homes have a wooden **હીંચકો** (swing) in the living room or on the veranda, where families sit and chat in the evening. Shoes are taken off at the door, and in traditional homes the kitchen and prayer area (મંદિર) are especially kept clean. Apartment blocks are called **સોસાયટી** *sosāyṭī* or **ફ્લૅટ**, and floors are counted from the ground floor (ગ્રાઉન્ડ ફ્લોર) upwards.

tip.title: 'There is' and -માં 'in'
tip.body:
- There's no separate 'there is': put the place first and end with **છે**: ઘરમાં હીંચકો **છે**.
- 'There isn't' is **નથી**; 'nobody' is **કોઈ નથી**.
- **-માં** 'in' joins the noun. -ો and -ું nouns change to -ા first: ઓરડો → **ઓરડામાં**, રસોડું → **રસોડામાં**.

sentences.en: There are two bathrooms in our house.
There's a swing at Grandma's house.
How many rooms are there in your house?

lessons.title: On the table, under the bed

tip.title: In, on, under
tip.body:
- Postpositions come **after** the noun: ટેબલ **પર** 'on the table', કબાટ**માં** 'in the cupboard'.
- **ઉપર** 'on top of' and **નીચે** 'under' take **-ની** first: ખુરશી**ની નીચે** 'under the chair'.
- Don't put -નો or -નું before them: always **-ની**.

sentences.en: The bag is on the bed.
The bag is under the table.
Your bag is in the cupboard.
What's on top of the cupboard?
Your tea is on the table.

sentences.native: તારો ફોન ત્યાં છે, પલંગ પર.
sentences.roman: tāro fon tyāṃ chhe, palaṅg par.
sentences.en: Your phone is over there, on the bed.
The book isn't in the cupboard.
There's no window in this room.

sentences.native: ભીંત પર મારા દાદાનો ફોટો છે.
sentences.roman: bhīṃt par mārā dādāno foṭo chhe.
sentences.en: There's a photo of my grandfather on the wall.
The phone isn't here — look over there.

tip.title: Next to, behind — and 'I have it'
tip.body:
- **પાસે** near, **પાછળ** behind, **આગળ** in front, **સામે** opposite, **બાજુમાં** next to — all take **-ની**: ઘર**ની પાછળ**.
- **મારી પાસે** = 'near me', and also 'I have (on me)': મારી પાસે ચાવી છે.
- So **તમારી પાસે … છે?** = 'Do you have …?'

sentences.en: Have you got a phone on you? (to a friend)

sentences.native: અમારા ઘરની સામે એક દુકાન છે.
sentences.roman: amārā gharnī sāme ek dukān chhe.
sentences.en: There's a shop opposite our house.
The kitchen is at the back of the house.
The chair is next to the window.

sentences.native: મારા મિત્રનું ઘર બીજે માળે છે.
sentences.roman: mārā mitranuṃ ghar bīje māḷe chhe.
sentences.en: My friend's flat is on the second floor.
All the kids are in front of the house.

The dishes are in the kitchen.
There are lots of dishes in the kitchen.
